# dsh-superpowers
English | 中文

obra/superpowers (v7.0.1) ported to the
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) as a profile bundle.

Installs the 15 Superpowers process skills and injects the
`using-superpowers` bootstrap at every se

ssion start — no per-session opt-in,
following the Superpowers porting guide

## What it does

- Registers every vendored `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as a runtime skill on
`ctx.skills`, so the harne

ss catalog lists them and the native `skill` tool
can load them. Each skill's resources resolve insi

de its own directory.
- Registers a system-prompt section (`superpowers:bootstrap`) containing the
`

using-superpowers` skill body wrapped in `<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>`, plus a
DeepSeek Harness tool mappi

ng (`skill`/`read`/`write`/`edit`/`glob`/`grep`/
`pwsh`/`subagent`/`todo_write`/`ask_user_question`/

`web_search`/`web_fetch`/
`read_image`/`dsh_browser_*`). Sections re-assemble before every model ste

p,
so the bootstrap needs no dedup guard and survives compaction.
- Zero runtime dependencies.
## Feature parity
Everything in obra/superpowers that applies at runtime is replicated here:
| Upstream capability | In this bundle |
| 15 skills, 84 files (SKILL.md + references / scripts / prompts / templates) | Vendored verbatim —
the `skills/` tree is file-for-file hash-identical to upstream v7.0.1, except the two changes the po

rting guide sanctions (see Attribution) |
| Session-start bootstrap (`using-superpowers` wrapped in
`<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>`) | A system-prompt section, re-assembled before every model step — no dedup

guard needed and it survives compaction |
| Per-harness tool mapping (`references/<harness>-tools.md
`) | `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md`, linked from the Platform Adaptation list an

d inlined in the bootstrap |
| Skill sub-resources (references, scripts, prompts, templates) | Each

skill's resource base points at its own directory; files load with the `read` tool |
| Bundled scrip
ts (`*.sh`, `*.cjs`, `*.js`) | Run through their interpreter (`bash`, `node`); on Windows, Git Bash

provides `bash` (watch for the WSL launcher shadowing it on PATH) |
| Subagent workflows (dispatchin

g-parallel-agents, subagent-driven-development) | DSH `subagent` / `subagent_fork` tools |
| Task tr

acking | `todo_write` |
| Web lookups (diagnosing-superpowers, brainstorming recon) | `web_search` /

`web_fetch` / the built-in browser |
| Git worktrees (using-git-worktrees) | System `git` from any

` / the built-in browser |
| Git worktrees (using-git-worktrees) | System `git` from any DSH shell |
Not shipped, matching what upstream's own per-harness distributions exclude: the other platforms' ma
nifests and hooks (`.claude-plugin/`, `hooks/`, …), marketplace metadata, and dev tooling (`tests/`,
`evals/`, release scripts). Those are install machinery for other harnesses; their DSH equivalents
are this bundle's `index.js` and `cordis.patch.yml`.

Verified with the upstream acceptance test: in a fresh session, the prompt
"Let's make a react todo
list" auto-invokes `brainstorming` before any code.

## Attribution & scope of changes

The `skills/` directory is vendored verbatim from
obra/superpowers (MIT, © Jesse Vincent)
— skill bo

dies are not modified, per the upstream contributor rules. The only
additions are a one-line DeepSee

k Harness entry in
`skills/using-superpowers/SKILL.md`'s Platform Adaptation pointer list and the
ne

w `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md` tool mapping, both
explicitly allowed by the po

rting guide.
The DSH integration layer (`index.js`, `cordis.patch.yml`, locale files, icon)
is new c
ode, MIT, © 2026 Huoris. See LICENSE.
